# BeyondRetarget Testing Records

Date: 2026-10-18. Conclusion: **Video generation using the official online service by the Eight Robot action system has been implemented; local GPU inference, training, SONIC dynamics tracking, and real robot control have not been verified.**

[ New method comparison page ](../comparison.md) uses author's paper data and official demonstrations, and provides a local baseline re-run process; four GVHMR/WHAM → GMR/NMR baselines have not been actually run. The GVHMR input entry of GMR, NMR input/output documents, and their online interfaces have been verified, but these interfaces are not considered as baseline experiments.

## Input and Sources

- Input source: [ provides a video demonstration ](https://weixin.qq.com/sph/A9gBA1DBZ6), and the research work is [ BeyondRetarget ](https://bear-ty.github.io/Beyondretarget_page/) by teams such as Nanjing University.
- The original video has been confirmed to be downloaded locally: 720×1280, 78.75 seconds, H.264 / AAC.
- Take the 2–8 seconds, extract only the full-body image of the person on the left, with a cropping size of 178×306 and the upper-left corner `(0,534)`. Resample to 30 FPS, remove audio track, and use H.264 CRF 18. The original video and the input crop are not released along with the tutorial.
- Input SHA256: `4f425867086a0eede218a671748ce14666a1fbf53b21e767f7e3be6fa0bb2d69`.

The input preparation command is as follows: `source.mp4` is the original video obtained by the reader. If the platform replaces the video aspect ratio later, the cropping area must be re-verified, and the coordinates should not be copied verbatim:

```bash
ffmpeg -ss 2 -i source.mp4 -t 6 -vf "crop=178:306:0:534,fps=30" -an -c:v libx264 -crf 18 person_6s.mp4
```

The character pool in this material is limited, mainly consisting of standing postures and hand movements. This example verifies service invocation and data export, but it is not an independent test set, a quantitative reproduction experiment, or a verification of the paper's generalization ability.

## Running Environment and Version

- Client: Windows, Python 3.12, `gradio_client==1.13.3`, `numpy==1.26.4`.
- Inference device: Official Hugging Face ZeroGPU service; no local GPU is used.
- Space: `bear-ty/BeyondRetarget`; verify the public shell SHA: `13eef4dde553ff96a39c7129291ef70c9a31fcef`. The version of the private runtime package is not publicly available, so it is impossible to infer its internal model from this. The corresponding version on GitHub cannot be determined.
- The two stages are called in the same session order: `/zero_gpu_inference` → `/finish_cpu_stage`.
- Start time: 20:24:47, Beijing Time, October 18, 2026; total time is approximately 179.78 seconds, including network, queue, GPU inference, CPU rendering, and downloading. It is not purely model-related delay.
- Local steps only involve checking the entry and resource definitions of the upstream commit `e0331d0faf9091095bae9100e03655c944e2b64a`. When performing environment detection, there are only about 2 GB of VRAM available on the laboratory GPU, and no inference is started or other tasks are modified.

The above dimensions represent the actual observations of online service products, and do not replace the configurations of local robots. The file name prefix for GR2/H1 is also different from the local CLI names. There are no contact predictions or independent post-processing data in the ZIP file, so this record does not claim to verify the post-processing process within the service.

There are eight robots and posture changes visible in the key frames. The robots are placed in the same scene replay, so it cannot be concluded that gravity, support contact, or closed loop tracking is established. There are no real robot/human truth values, foot contact annotations, or tracking controller logs, hence MAMPJPE, foot slip metrics, latency benchmarks, or execution success rates are not reported.

## Tutorial Code Verification

Execute from this chapter directory:

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'
python scripts/inspect_motion.py results/motions.zip
```

- Six sets of unit tests passed: valid original actions, anomaly prediction, valid body export, incorrect contact data input, object arrays, and corrupted files.
- Eight sets of real reasoning data in this chapter passed the check.
- The client actually completed two-stage calls and file saving; input checks for the 78.75-second original video were rejected before uploading, and no output directory was created.
- The tutorial directory was included in the e-book directory, and the text was generated into HTML by the existing Markdown renderer; relative link checks for this chapter passed.
